title: MEDEC: A Benchmark for Medical Error Detection and Correction in Clinical Notes

paper.authors: Ben Abacha, Yim, Fu, Sun, Yetisgen, Xia, Lin (Microsoft Health & Life Sciences AI / University of Washington)
paper.repo_note: Scaffold had cloned only third-party tools (philter, QuickUMLS); the paper's own repos were cloned for this card. 'medec-exps' in MEDEC is a PNG, not code.

dependence.note: The benchmark paper's central result is how well LLMs detect/correct injected errors relative to two medical doctors; all model rows in Tables 2-4 are LLM outputs scored automatically.

claim.statement: On the 925-note MEDEC test set with the zero-shot prompt P#1, GPT-4o reached error-flag accuracy 0.6584 and error-sentence accuracy 0.5665 (correction AggregateScore 0.4682) and GPT-4 0.6573 / 0.5568 (0.5751); the best LLM (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, 0.7016 / 0.6562) stayed below both medical doctors (0.7961 / 0.6588 and 0.7161 / 0.6677) - 'recent LLMs are still outperformed by medical doctors' (Table 2).
claim.metric: accuracy of error-flag prediction (subtask A) and error-sentence identification (subtask B) over 925 test texts; correction quality on flagged texts via ROUGE-1, BERTScore (deberta-xlarge-mnli), BLEURT, their AggregateScore, and MIST/MIST-COMB
claim.original_source: Table 2 (full 925-text test set; * = P#2 prompt); Table 3 (MS/UW split - reported only for Claude 3.5 Sonnet and o1-preview); Table 4 (recall by error type); Section 5.4

protocol.model_note: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 is the only dated live snapshot in the paper, but Section 5.1 attaches it to 'GPT-4o-mini (gpt-4o-2024-05-13)' - it is ambiguous whether it denotes the GPT-4o row or the GPT-4o-mini row of Table 2. 'GPT-4' is cited via the docs page 'gpt-4-turbo-and-gpt-4' (accessed 03/2024) with no snapshot; the scaffold's 'gpt-4-turbo' is inferred, not stated. Also used: o1-mini-2024-09-12 and o1-preview-2024-09-12 (dead), Claude 3.5 Sonnet 2024-10-22 (dead), Gemini 2.0 Flash, DeepSeek-R1 (Azure AI Foundry), Phi-3-7B, ChatGPT.
protocol.model_status: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 dying 2026-10-23; gpt-4-turbo dying 2026-10-23 (unverified as the paper's 'GPT-4')
protocol.endpoint: OpenAI chat completions (provider/route not stated for OpenAI models; DeepSeek-R1 via Azure AI Foundry)
protocol.prompt_source: Paper Section 4, verbatim P#1 ('The following is a medical narrative about a patient. You are a skilled medical doctor reviewing the clinical text. The text is either correct or contains one error ... If the text is correct return the following output: CORRECT. If the text has a medical error ... return the sentence id ... followed by a space, and then a corrected version of the sentence ...') and P#2 (P#1 + one randomly selected training example, quoted in the paper)

params.other: input = note with one sentence per line prefixed by sentence ID; minimal post-processing for Phi-3/Claude formatting

protocol.n_items_note: 597 MS (public) + 328 UW (DUA); Table 2 values are on all 925
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: parse 'CORRECT' vs '<sentence_id> <corrected sentence>'; flag/sentence accuracy; NLG metrics via MEDIQA-CORR-2024/evaluation/mediqa-corr-2024-eval-script-2-all-metrics.py (ROUGE-1, BERTScore, BLEURT, AggregateScore); MIST requires UMLS + scispaCy en_core_sci_scibert

artifacts.prompts_note: verbatim in the paper (Section 4); not in the repo
artifacts.data_license: CC BY 4.0 (MEDEC-MS); UW under Data Use Agreement
artifacts.notes: MS notes are MedQA-derived vignettes with injected errors (possibly seen in pre-training); UW notes are real de-identified hospital notes never released publicly. A cleaned copy exists at huggingface.co/datasets/mkieffer/MEDEC (authors recommend the original for comparisons).

blockers: Table 2 reference values are on the full 925-note test set; the 328 UW notes require a UW DUA - without it only the 597-note MS subset can be run, and MS-only reference values for GPT-4/GPT-4o are not reported (Table 3 covers only Claude and o1-preview)
model snapshot ambiguity: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 is labelled 'GPT-4o-mini' in the paper text; 'GPT-4' has no snapshot
generation parameters (temperature, max tokens) not reported
MIST metric needs a UMLS licence and scispaCy models; BLEURT/BERTScore checkpoints must be pinned

budget.assumptions: MS test only (597 notes) x 3 seeds for gpt-4o-2024-05-13; ~650 input tokens (note + P#1) and ~80 output tokens. A second gpt-4-turbo arm adds ~USD 16 (total ~USD 24); running the full 925 with the UW DUA scales by 1.55x (~USD 37 for both arms).

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1: for the live arm, error-flag and error-sentence accuracy within +/- 0.05 of the Table 2 values (bootstrap CI over notes) - flagged 'subset' if only MS is available; the direction claim 'best LLM < both doctors on flag accuracy' (0.70 vs 0.72-0.80) must hold with successor arms; correction AggregateScore judged by direction only.
judgment.notes: Chance level for error-flag accuracy is ~0.5 (51.3% of notes have errors); doctors' IAA was only 69% (flag) / 58% (sentence).

user_checks: Which Table 2 row is gpt-4o-2024-05-13 - 'GPT-4o' (0.6584 / 0.5665) or 'GPT-4o-mini' (0.6086 / 0.4757)? The paper text conflates them; ask abenabacha@microsoft.com.
Apply for the UW DUA to match the 925-note test set, or accept MS-only (597) with an explicit 'subset' flag in the judgment?
Treat 'GPT-4' as gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 at all, given the paper never names the snapshot?
domain_notes: Each note is either correct or contains exactly one injected error of five types (diagnosis, management, treatment, pharmacotherapy, causal organism); MS notes were built by rewriting MedQA board-exam vignettes with a plausible wrong answer, UW notes by medical students editing real diagnosis-support notes. The human ceiling is noisy (doctor IAA 69%/58%), and o1-preview showed very high recall but hallucinated errors (low precision), so 'LLM vs doctor' comparisons hinge on accuracy, not recall. The MS/UW gap for o1-preview (73% vs 58% flag accuracy) suggests MedQA-derived notes are partly memorised - a contamination caveat for any GPT-4-class arm.
decisions_2026_09_18: Table 2 row 'GPT-4o' (0.6584 / 0.5665) is the primary comparison for gpt-4o-2024-05-13; the 'GPT-4o-mini' row is recorded as an alternative cell
MS test subset only (597 notes), judgment flagged 'subset'; no UW DUA
the unpinned 'GPT-4' arm is not run; the card has one live model, gpt-4o-2024-05-13
